definition: all the people who are employed in a company, industry or country
example: A well-trained workforce is the most valuable asset a growing manufacturing firm can have.

definition: loss of a job because an employer no longer needs the worker
example: Many older employees faced redundancy when the factory closed its second production line.

definition: to find and employ new people for an organisation
example: The hospital plans to recruit fifty additional nurses before the start of winter.

definition: a person who formally asks for a job or a place on a course
example: Each applicant must submit a short cover letter along with their application form.

definition: a short period of work experience, often unpaid, done to gain skills
example: An internship at a law firm gave her a realistic picture of daily office routines.

definition: a period of paid training in which a young person learns a skilled trade
example: An apprenticeship allows school leavers to earn a wage while acquiring practical qualifications.

definition: a person you work with in the same organisation
example: My colleagues often organise lunch together, which makes the office feel less formal.

definition: a person who watches over workers and checks their performance
example: Her supervisor reviews every report before it is sent to the client.

definition: relating to the work of running a business or a team
example: Promotion to a managerial post often requires skills that technical training does not provide.

definition: a person who starts a business and takes financial risks to do so
example: Many young entrepreneurs struggle to obtain a loan because they lack collateral.

definition: working for yourself instead of for an employer
example: Being self-employed offers freedom, but income can fluctuate sharply from one month to the next.

definition: working for different companies on separate jobs rather than for one employer
example: A freelance translator can choose her clients but has no paid holiday or sick leave.

definition: a system in which workers choose their own start and finish times within agreed limits
example: Flexitime enables parents to drop their children at school before travelling to the office.

definition: the likelihood that a person will keep their job without the risk of dismissal
example: Public sector posts are popular among graduates because they offer greater job security.

definition: a healthy division of time and energy between paid work and personal life
paraphrases: balance between job and private life
example: Employees who enjoy a sound work-life balance tend to take fewer sick days.

definition: a state of physical and mental exhaustion caused by long-term stress at work
example: Nurses working double shifts for months are particularly vulnerable to burnout.

definition: extra hours worked beyond normal working hours
example: Staff were asked to work overtime during the busy period before the holidays.

definition: the amount of work that a person has to do
example: A heavy workload and tight deadlines left many teachers feeling overwhelmed.

definition: the rate at which workers produce goods or complete tasks compared with the effort used
example: Shorter meetings and clearer goals have raised productivity across the department.

definition: to make a process or organisation simpler and more efficient
example: The company hopes to streamline its hiring procedures by removing two stages of interviews.

definition: to give part of your work or authority to someone else
example: Good managers know when to delegate rather than trying to control every detail themselves.

definition: to pay another company to do work that was previously done inside your own organisation
example: Many firms outsource customer service to call centres in countries with lower labour costs.

definition: to reduce the number of people employed by a company in order to cut costs
example: Facing falling sales, the retailer was forced to downsize and close several branches.

definition: to officially remove someone from their job
example: An employee cannot be dismissed without a written warning and a chance to improve.

definition: to formally announce that you are leaving your job
example: He decided to resign after the board rejected his proposal for the third time.

definition: regular money paid to a person after they stop working because of age
example: Many self-employed people do not contribute to a pension and rely on savings instead.

definition: an organisation of workers formed to protect their rights and interests
example: The trade union negotiated a pay rise on behalf of its members.

definition: negotiation between employers and a group of workers about pay and conditions
example: Collective bargaining gives low-paid staff greater influence over their working conditions.

definition: the lowest hourly pay that employers are legally allowed to give
example: Critics argue that raising the minimum wage could discourage small firms from hiring.

definition: the difference in average earnings between two groups of workers
example: The gender pay gap persists partly because women are more likely to work part-time.

definition: an unseen barrier that prevents some groups, especially women, from reaching top positions
example: Despite equal qualifications, many women still hit the glass ceiling before reaching the boardroom.

definition: unfair treatment of a person because of their age, sex, race or other characteristic
example: Laws against discrimination require employers to judge applicants on skills rather than on background.

definition: the place such as an office or factory where people do their jobs
example: Clear safety rules in the workplace have reduced accidents in the construction industry.

definition: a person's job or profession
example: Applicants must state their current occupation and the name of their employer.

definition: an exam, course or certificate that shows you are able to do a job
example: A professional qualification in accounting greatly improves a candidate's chances of promotion.

definition: special skill or knowledge in a particular field
example: The agency hired a consultant whose expertise in tax law saved it thousands of pounds.

definition: having the skills and knowledge needed to do a job well
example: A competent engineer should be able to identify the fault within a few minutes.

definition: able to do something skilfully because of training or practice
example: Candidates should be proficient in spreadsheet software and basic data analysis.

definition: showing careful and steady effort in your work
example: A diligent employee usually checks each figure twice before submitting a financial report.

definition: careful to do work thoroughly and correctly
example: Conscientious staff rarely need close supervision because they take pride in accurate work.

definition: something that encourages a person to work harder or do a particular thing
example: Cash bonuses act as an incentive for sales staff to exceed their monthly targets.

definition: an extra benefit given to an employee in addition to a salary
example: Free gym membership and subsidised meals are popular perks at the technology firm.

definition: an extra payment given to an employee for good work or good company results
example: Each member of the team received a bonus after the company exceeded its annual targets.

definition: payment given to a person for their work
example: Executives' remuneration has risen much faster than the average worker's earnings.

definition: requiring a lot of effort, skill or time
example: Emergency medicine is a demanding career that leaves little time for family life.

definition: involving the same action done again and again
example: Factory staff often complain that repetitive tasks make the working day feel endless.

definition: dull and unchanging, so that you become bored
example: Data entry can be monotonous, so many firms rotate staff between different tasks.

definition: giving personal satisfaction because you feel the work is worthwhile
example: Teaching is not well paid, but many people find it deeply rewarding.

definition: making you feel happy because you are using your abilities
example: A fulfilling job matters more to many graduates than a high starting salary.

definition: respected and admired because of high status
example: A prestigious post at an international firm can open many doors later in a career.

definition: not secure or safe, and likely to end suddenly
example: Seasonal staff often live in a precarious situation, never sure of work beyond the summer.

definition: needing a large amount of human work rather than machinery
example: Textile manufacturing is a labour-intensive industry that employs millions in developing economies.

definition: physical work done with the hands, such as building or farming
example: Years of manual labour on construction sites had damaged his back.

definition: relating to workers who do office or professional work
example: White-collar employees now make up the majority of the workforce in most wealthy countries.

definition: relating to workers who do physical work in factories or similar places
example: Blue-collar jobs in mining have declined sharply as machines took over dangerous tasks.

definition: work that takes place at set periods, often including nights and weekends
example: Long periods of shift work can disrupt sleep and make family meals hard to arrange.

definition: the feeling of being pleased with your work and working conditions
example: Surveys show that job satisfaction depends more on relationships with colleagues than on salary.

definition: the chances of future progress and success in your working life
example: A master's degree can significantly improve career prospects in the engineering sector.

definition: the series of ranks through which a worker can rise during their working life
example: She started at the bottom of the career ladder as a receptionist and became a director within ten years.

definition: to approach a skilled person who already has a job and offer them a new one
example: The software company tried to headhunt several engineers from its main competitor.

definition: to put someone on a list of the best candidates from whom a final choice will be made
example: Only six of the two hundred applicants were shortlisted for interview.

definition: a person who is being asked questions in an interview
example: A confident interviewee maintains eye contact and answers questions clearly.

definition: the combined effort of a group of people working together
example: Successful teamwork depends on trust, and trust grows when people share clear goals.

definition: to work jointly with other people on a shared project
example: Engineers and designers must collaborate closely if a product is to meet customer needs.

definition: to discuss something formally in order to reach an agreement
example: New graduates are often reluctant to negotiate a higher starting salary.

definition: a formal review of how well an employee has done their job
example: A fair performance appraisal should include both praise and specific advice on how to improve.

definition: the rate at which employees leave an organisation and are replaced
example: High staff turnover is costly because every new recruit must be trained from the beginning.

definition: the habit of regularly staying away from work without good reason
example: Absenteeism fell sharply after the firm introduced flexible working hours.

definition: a long period of paid leave from work, often used for study or travel
example: After seven years of teaching, she took a sabbatical to write a book.

definition: having no paid employment
example: Jobless young people often lose confidence the longer they remain without a position.

definition: to end the employment of workers, usually because there is not enough work
example: The company had to lay off two hundred workers when demand for its products fell.

definition: a labour market in which people take short-term or freelance jobs rather than permanent posts
example: The gig economy offers flexibility but gives workers little protection against sudden loss of income.
